children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text: mano hi dvividhaṃ proktaṃ śuddhaṃ cāśuddham eva ca /
children.translated_text: The mind is said to be of two kinds: pure and impure.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ kāmasaṃkalpaṃ śuddhaṃ kāmavivarjitam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: The impure is that which is tainted by desire and intention; the pure is that which is free from desire. (1)

children.text: mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings.

children.text: bandhāya viṣayāsaktaṃ muktyai nirviṣayaṃ smṛtam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Attached to sense-objects, it leads to bondage; free from sense-objects, it is remembered as [leading to] liberation. (2)

children.text: yato nirviṣayasyāsya manaso muktir iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Since liberation is desired for the mind that is free from sense-objects,

children.text: tasmān nirviṣayaṃ nityaṃ manaḥ kāryaṃ mumukṣuṇā || 3 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the seeker of liberation should always make the mind free from sense-objects. (3)

children.text: nirastaviṣayāsaṅgaṃ saṃniruddhaṃ mano hṛdi /
children.translated_text: When the mind, freed from attachment to sense-objects and restrained in the heart,

children.text: yadā yāty unmanībhāvaṃ tadā tat paramamadam || 4 ||
children.translated_text: attains the state beyond mind (<s>unmanībhāva</s>), then that is the supreme bliss. (4)

children.text: tāvad eva niroddhavyaṃ yāvaddhṛdi gataṃ kṣayam /
children.translated_text: It should be restrained until it reaches dissolution in the heart.

children.text: etaj jñānaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca ato 'nyo granthavistaraḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: This is knowledge and this is liberation; all else is mere expansion of texts. (5)

children.text: naiva cintyaṃ na cācintyam acintyaṃ cintyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Neither to be thought upon, nor not to be thought upon; the unthinkable is indeed to be thought upon.

children.text: pakṣapātavinirmuktaṃ brahma sampadyate tadā || 6 ||
children.translated_text: When free from all partiality, <s>Brahman</s> is then attained. (6)

children.text: svareṇa saṃdhayed yogam asvaraṃ bhāvayet param /
children.translated_text: Through sound (<s>svara</s>), one should practice <s>yoga</s>; the supreme should be contemplated as beyond sound.

children.text: asvareṇa hi bhāvena bhāvo nābhāva iṣyate || 7 ||
children.translated_text: Through contemplation of the soundless, true being arises, not non-being. (7)

children.text: tad eva niṣkalaṃ brahma nirvikalpaṃ nirañjanam /
children.translated_text: That itself is the partless <s>Brahman</s>, without mental constructions, unstained.

children.text: tad brahmāham iti jñātvā brahma sampadyate dhruvam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: Knowing 'I am that <s>Brahman</s>,' one certainly attains <s>Brahman</s>. (8)

children.text: nirvikalpam anantaṃ ca hetudṛṣṭāntavarjitam /
children.translated_text: Without mental constructions, infinite, devoid of reasoning and illustration,

children.text: aprameyam anādyaṃ ca jñātvā ca paramaṃ śivam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: immeasurable, beginningless — knowing the supreme <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One). (9)

children.text: na nirodho na cotpattir na vandyo na ca śāsanam /
children.translated_text: There is no cessation, no arising, no one in bondage, no spiritual discipline,

children.text: na mumukṣā na muktiś ca ity eṣā paramārthatā || 10 ||
children.translated_text: no seeker of liberation, no liberation — this is the ultimate truth. (10)

children.text: eka evātmā mantavyo jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu /
children.translated_text: The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) alone should be known in waking, dream, and deep sleep.

children.text: sthānatrayād vyatītasya punarjanma na vidyate || 11 ||
children.translated_text: For one who has transcended the three states, there is no rebirth. (11)

children.text: eka eva hi bhūtātmā bhūte bhūte vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The one Self of beings is established in each and every being.

children.text: ekadhā bahudhā caiva dṛśyate jalacandravat || 12 ||
children.translated_text: It is seen as one and as many, like the moon reflected in water. (12)

children.text: ghaṭasaṃbhṛtam ākāśaṃ līyamāne ghaṭe yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the space enclosed in a pot — when the pot is dissolved,

children.text: ghaṭo līyeta nākāśaṃ tadvaj jīvo ghaṭopamaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: the pot dissolves, not the space — so the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) is like the pot. (13)

children.text: ghaṭavad vividhākāraṃ bhidyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a pot, taking on various forms, being broken again and again —

children.text: tadbhagnaṃ na ca jānāti sa jānāti ca nityaśaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: it does not know that which is broken, but It (the Self) knows eternally. (14)

children.text: śabdamāyāvṛto yāvat tāvat tiṣṭhati puṣkare /
children.translated_text: As long as one is enveloped by the illusion of words, so long one remains in the lotus [of the heart].

children.text: bhinne tamasi caikatvam ekam evānupaśyati || 15 ||
children.translated_text: When the darkness is pierced, one sees the one unity alone. (15)

children.text: śabdākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma yasmin kṣīṇe yad akṣaram /
children.translated_text: The word-syllable (<s>śabdākṣara</s>) is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; when it is exhausted, that which is imperishable remains.

children.text: tad vidvān akṣaraṃ dhyāyed yadīcchecchāntim ātmanaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: The wise one should meditate on the imperishable, if one desires peace for the self. (16)

children.text: dve vidye veditavye tu śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: Two kinds of knowledge are to be known: <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (Word-Brahman) and the supreme beyond it.

children.text: śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati || 17 ||
children.translated_text: One who is proficient in <s>Śabdabrahman</s> attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. (17)

children.text: grantham abhyasya medhāvī jñānavijñānatattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one, having studied the texts with [the aim of gaining] knowledge and realization,

children.text: palālam iva dhānyārthī tyajed grantham aśeṣataḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: should discard all texts entirely, as one seeking grain discards the chaff. (18)

children.text: gavām anekavarṇānāṃ kṣīrasyāpy ekavarṇatā /
children.translated_text: Of cows of various colors, the milk is of one color alone.

children.text: kṣīravat paśyate jñānaṃ liṅginas tu gavāṃ yathā || 19 ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge is seen like the milk; the embodied beings are like the cows. (19)

children.text: ghṛtam iva payasi nigūḍhaṃ bhūte bhūte ca vasati vijñānam /
children.translated_text: Like ghee hidden in milk, consciousness dwells in every being.

children.text: satataṃ manthayitavyaṃ manasā manthānabhūtena || 20 ||
children.translated_text: It should be constantly churned with the mind as the churning stick. (20)

children.text: jñānanetraṃ samādāya cared vahnim ataḥ param /
children.translated_text: Taking knowledge as the eye, one should extract the fire beyond.

children.text: niṣkalaṃ nirmalaṃ śāntaṃ tad brahmāham iti smṛtam || 21 ||
children.translated_text: Partless, pure, peaceful — 'I am that <s>Brahman</s>' is the established teaching. (21)

children.text: sarvabhūtādhivāsaṃ ca yad bhūteṣu vasaty adhi /
children.translated_text: That which is the dwelling place of all beings, and which dwells within all beings,

children.text: sarvānugrāhakatvena tad asmy ahaṃ vāsudeva || 22 ||
children.translated_text: by being the benefactor of all — 'I am that <s>Vāsudeva</s>.' (22)
